answer: When a fault strikes a feeder, recorders at both ends stamp it within microseconds, so a claimant reports the fault transient it observed and its timestamp must match the recorder log for that feeder. A lagoon of fake claims fails because faults are rare, unpredictable and publicly logged after the fact, leaving no time to fabricate a matching transient; a wharf side recorder and a bridge side recorder agree, and the transient's shape differs per feeder, so one farm recording cannot serve many feeders.
